sanskrit: kasya putraḥ sa rājāsīt sarpasatraṃ ya āharat sa ca dvijātipravaraḥ kasya putro vadasva me
english: Whose son was that king who performed the serpent sacrifice? And that foremost of the twice-born — whose son was he? Tell me this.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mahad ākhyānam āstīkaṃ yatraitat procyate dvija sarvam etad aśeṣeṇa śṛṇu me vadatāṃ vara
english: The Sūta said: The great legend called Āstīka, in which all this is proclaimed — O brahmin, best among speakers, hear it all from me without remainder.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca śrotum icchāmy aśeṣeṇa kathām etāṃ manoramām āstīkasya purāṇasya brāhmaṇasya yaśasvinaḥ
english: Śaunaka said: I wish to hear in full this delightful tale of Āstīka, that ancient brahmin of glorious renown.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca itihāsam imaṃ vṛddhāḥ purāṇaṃ paricakṣate kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaproktaṃ naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ
english: The Sūta said: The elders who dwell in the Naimiṣa forest recount this as an ancient tale of sacred history, spoken by Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ pracoditaḥ sūtaḥ pitā me lomaharṣaṇaḥ śiṣyo vyāsasya medhāvī brāhmaṇair idam uktavān
english: Formerly, urged on by the brahmins, my father Lomaharṣaṇa the Sūta, that wise disciple of Vyāsa, narrated this very tale.

sanskrit: tasmād aham upaśrutya pravakṣyāmi yathātatham idam āstīkam ākhyānaṃ tubhyaṃ śaunaka pṛcchate
english: Having heard it from him, I shall now tell this Āstīka legend to you exactly as it is, O Śaunaka who inquires of me.

sanskrit: āstīkasya pitā hy āsīt prajāpatisamaḥ prabhuḥ brahmacārī yatāhāras tapasy ugre rataḥ sadā
english: The father of Āstīka was a lord equal to Prajāpati himself — a celibate student, restrained in food, ever devoted to fierce austerity.

sanskrit: jaratkārur iti khyāta ūrdhvaretā mahān ṛṣiḥ yāyāvarāṇāṃ dharmajñaḥ pravaraḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Known as Jaratkāru, he was a great seer of upward-flowing seed, foremost among the Yāyāvaras who knew the law, firm in his vow.

sanskrit: aṭamānaḥ kadā cit sa svān dadarśa pitāmahān lambamānān mahāgarte pādair ūrdhvair adhomukhān
english: Wandering once, he saw his own forefathers hanging in a great pit, their feet pointing upward and their faces downward.

sanskrit: tān abravīt sa dṛṣṭvaiva jaratkāruḥ pitāmahān ke bhavanto 'valambante garte 'smin vā adhomukhāḥ
english: Upon seeing them, Jaratkāru spoke to those forefathers: "Who are you who hang here in this pit, faces downward?"

sanskrit: vīraṇastambake lagnāḥ sarvataḥ paribhakṣite mūṣakena nigūḍhena garte 'smin nityavāsinā
english: Clinging to a clump of vīraṇa grass gnawed away on all sides by a hidden mouse that dwells perpetually in this pit.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ yāyāvarā nāma vayam ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ saṃtānaprakṣayād brahmann adho gacchāma medinīm
english: The forefathers said: We are sages of the Yāyāvara lineage, firm in our vows. O brahmin, due to the extinction of our line we are sinking into the earth.

sanskrit: asmākaṃ saṃtatis tv eko jaratkārur iti śrutaḥ mandabhāgyo 'lpabhāgyānāṃ tapa eva samāsthitaḥ
english: Our single descendant is known as Jaratkāru — the most ill-fated among the ill-fated; he has taken refuge only in asceticism.

sanskrit: na sa putrāñ janayituṃ dārān mūḍhaś cikīrṣati tena lambāmahe garte saṃtānaprakṣayād iha
english: That fool does not wish to take a wife or beget sons. Because of this extinction of lineage we hang here in the pit.

sanskrit: anāthās tena nāthena yathā duṣkṛtinas tathā kas tvaṃ bandhur ivāsmākam anuśocasi sattama
english: Bereft of that protector, we are like sinners without a refuge. Who are you, good sir, who grieves for us as though a kinsman?

sanskrit: jñātum icchāmahe brahman ko bhavān iha dhiṣṭhitaḥ kimarthaṃ caiva naḥ śocyān anukampitum arhasi
english: We wish to know, O brahmin — who are you who stands here? And why do you take pity on us who are so pitiable?

sanskrit: jaratkārur uvāca mama pūrve bhavanto vai pitaraḥ sapitāmahāḥ brūta kiṃ karavāṇy adya jaratkārur ahaṃ svayam
english: Jaratkāru said: You are truly my forefathers, my fathers and their fathers before them. Tell me — what shall I do? I am Jaratkāru himself.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ yatasva yatnavāṃs tāta saṃtānāya kulasya naḥ ātmano 'rthe 'smadarthe ca dharma ity eva cābhibho
english: The forefathers said: Strive diligently, dear son, for the continuation of our lineage — for your own sake, for our sake, and for the sake of dharma, O dear one.

sanskrit: na hi dharmaphalais tāta na tapobhiḥ susaṃcitaiḥ tāṃ gatiṃ prāpnuvantīha putriṇo yāṃ vrajanti ha
english: For neither through the fruits of dharma, dear son, nor through austerities well accumulated do men attain here the state that those with sons attain.

sanskrit: tad dāragrahaṇe yatnaṃ saṃtatyāṃ ca manaḥ kuru putrakāsmanniyogāt tvam etan naḥ paramaṃ hitam
english: Therefore, dear son, by our command, direct your effort toward taking a wife and continuing the line — this is our highest good.

sanskrit: jaratkārur uvāca na dārān vai kariṣyāmi sadā me bhāvitaṃ manaḥ bhavatāṃ tu hitārthāya kariṣye dārasaṃgraham
english: Jaratkāru said: I had ever resolved never to take a wife; yet for your benefit I shall take one as a wife.

sanskrit: samayena ca kartāham anena vidhipūrvakam tathā yady upalapsyāmi kariṣye nānyathā tv aham
english: But I shall do so only on this condition and in accordance with the proper rite: only if I find one who is offered to me — I shall not do otherwise.

sanskrit: sanāmnī yā bhavitrī me ditsitā caiva bandhubhiḥ bhaikṣavat tām ahaṃ kanyām upayaṃsye vidhānataḥ
english: She who shall be my wife must bear the same name as I, must be freely given by her kinsmen; I shall accept that maiden as alms, according to the ordained rule.

sanskrit: daridrāya hi me bhāryāṃ ko dāsyati viśeṣataḥ pratigrahīṣye bhikṣāṃ tu yadi kaś cit pradāsyati
english: For who would give a wife to one as poor as I? Yet I shall accept her as alms if someone offers her.

sanskrit: evaṃ dārakriyāhetoḥ prayatiṣye pitāmahāḥ anena vidhinā śaśvan na kariṣye 'ham anyathā
english: Thus for the purpose of taking a wife I shall strive, O forefathers, by this rule alone — I shall never act otherwise.

sanskrit: tatra cotpatsyate jantur bhavatāṃ tāraṇāya vai śāśvataṃ sthānam āsādya modantāṃ pitaro mama
english: And a being shall be born of her for your deliverance. May my forefathers attain the eternal abode and rejoice.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tato niveśāya tadā sa vipraḥ saṃśitavrataḥ mahīṃ cacāra dārārthī na ca dārān avindata
english: The Sūta said: Thereupon that brahmin of firm vow roamed the earth in search of a wife for his dwelling, but found none.

sanskrit: sa kadā cid vanaṃ gatvā vipraḥ pitṛvacaḥ smaran cukrośa kanyābhikṣārthī tisro vācaḥ śanair iva
english: Once, going into a forest and remembering the words of his forefathers, seeking a maiden as alms, he called out softly three times.

sanskrit: taṃ vāsukiḥ pratyagṛhṇād udyamya bhaginīṃ tadā na sa tāṃ pratijagrāha na sanāmnīti cintayan
english: Vāsuki came forward and offered his sister to him. But he did not accept her, thinking she did not bear his name.

sanskrit: sanāmnīm udyatāṃ bhāryāṃ gṛhṇīyām iti tasya hi mano niviṣṭam abhavaj jaratkāror mahātmanaḥ
english: For the mind of that great-souled Jaratkāru was fixed on this: he would take only a bride who shared his name when she was offered.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahāprājño jaratkārur mahātapāḥ kiṃnāmnī bhaginīyaṃ te brūhi satyaṃ bhujaṃgama
english: Then the greatly wise Jaratkāru of mighty austerity spoke to him: "What is the name of this sister of yours? Tell me truly, O serpent."

sanskrit: vāsukir uvāca jaratkāro jaratkāruḥ svaseyam anujā mama tvadarthaṃ rakṣitā pūrvaṃ pratīcchemāṃ dvijottama
english: Vāsuki said: O Jaratkāru, this is Jaratkāru, my younger sister. She has been kept all along for your sake — accept her, best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca mātrā hi bhujagāḥ śaptāḥ pūrvaṃ brahmavidāṃ vara janamejayasya vo yajñe dhakṣyaty anilasārathiḥ
english: The Sūta said: For the serpents had been cursed of old by their mother, O best of those who know brahman — "At the sacrifice of Janamejaya, fire with the wind as its charioteer shall burn you."

sanskrit: tasya śāpasya śāntyarthaṃ pradadau pannagottamaḥ svasāram ṛṣaye tasmai suvratāya tapasvine
english: For the pacification of that curse, the foremost of serpents gave his sister to that ascetic sage of excellent vow.

sanskrit: sa ca tāṃ pratijagrāha vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā āstīko nāma putraś ca tasyāṃ jajñe mahātmanaḥ
english: He accepted her according to the rite prescribed by tradition, and from her was born a son of that great-souled one, named Āstīka.

sanskrit: tapasvī ca mahātmā ca vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ samaḥ sarvasya lokasya pitṛmātṛbhayāpahaḥ
english: He was an ascetic and a great soul, versed in the Vedas and their limbs, equal-minded toward all beings, and a remover of the fears of both his father's and mother's kin.

sanskrit: atha kālasya mahataḥ pāṇḍaveyo narādhipaḥ ājahāra mahāyajñaṃ sarpasatram iti śrutiḥ
english: Then, after a great span of time, the Pāṇḍava king, lord of men, performed the great sacrifice known as the serpent sacrifice — so the tradition declares.

sanskrit: tasmin pravṛtte satre tu sarpāṇām antakāya vai mocayām āsa taṃ śāpam āstīkaḥ sumahāyaśāḥ
english: While that sacrifice was in progress — designed as the destruction of the serpents — Āstīka of great renown released them from that curse.

sanskrit: nāgāṃś ca mātulāṃś caiva tathā cānyān sa bāndhavān pitṝṃś ca tārayām āsa saṃtatyā tapasā tathā vrataiś ca vividhair brahman svādhyāyaiś cānṛṇo 'bhavat
english: He delivered the serpents who were his maternal uncles and other kinsmen; he also delivered his paternal ancestors through his lineage, austerities, various vows, and sacred study, O brahmin, and thus became free from debt.

sanskrit: devāṃś ca tarpayām āsa yajñair vividhadakṣiṇaiḥ ṛṣīṃś ca brahmacaryeṇa saṃtatyā ca pitāmahān
english: He satisfied the gods with sacrifices and abundant fees, the seers with celibacy, and the forefathers with the continuation of the lineage.

sanskrit: apahṛtya guruṃ bhāraṃ pitṝṇāṃ saṃśitavrataḥ jaratkārur gataḥ svargaṃ sahitaḥ svaiḥ pitāmahaiḥ
english: Having removed the heavy burden from his forefathers, Jaratkāru of firm vow went to heaven together with his own ancestors.

sanskrit: āstīkaṃ ca sutaṃ prāpya dharmaṃ cānuttamaṃ muniḥ jaratkāruḥ sumahatā kālena svargam īyivān
english: Having obtained a son in Āstīka and having practiced the highest dharma, the sage Jaratkāru ascended to heaven after a very long time.

sanskrit: etad ākhyānam āstīkaṃ yathāvat kīrtitaṃ mayā prabrūhi bhṛguśārdūla kiṃ bhūyaḥ kathyatām iti
english: This Āstīka legend has been recounted by me exactly as it occurred. O tiger among Bhṛgus, tell me — what more shall be narrated?

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca saute kathaya tām etāṃ vistareṇa kathāṃ punaḥ āstīkasya kaveḥ sādhoḥ śuśrūṣā paramā hi naḥ
english: Śaunaka said: O Sauti, tell that tale again in detail. Our desire to hear the story of Āstīka, that wise and virtuous man, is very great.

sanskrit: madhuraṃ kathyate saumya ślakṣṇākṣarapadaṃ tvayā prīyāmahe bhṛśaṃ tāta pitevedaṃ prabhāṣase
english: You tell it sweetly, dear one, with smooth syllables and words; we are greatly pleased. Dear child, you speak just as your father did.

sanskrit: asmacchuśrūṣaṇe nityaṃ pitā hi niratas tava ācaṣṭaitad yathākhyānaṃ pitā te tvaṃ tathā vada
english: Your father was ever devoted to serving us and told this tale just as it should be told — tell it as he did.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca āyuṣyam idam ākhyānam āstīkaṃ kathayāmi te yathā śrutaṃ kathayataḥ sakāśād vai pitur mayā
english: The Sūta said: This life-bestowing Āstīka legend I now tell you exactly as I heard it from my father while he narrated it.

sanskrit: purā devayuge brahman prajāpatisute śubhe āstāṃ bhaginyau rūpeṇa samupete 'dbhute 'naghe
english: In ancient times, O brahmin, in the age of the gods, two daughters of Prajāpati lived — sisters endowed with wondrous, matchless beauty, sinless.

sanskrit: te bhārye kaśyapasyāstāṃ kadrūś ca vinatā ca ha prādāt tābhyāṃ varaṃ prītaḥ prajāpatisamaḥ patiḥ kaśyapo dharmapatnībhyāṃ mudā paramayā yutaḥ
english: They were the wives of Kaśyapa — Kadrū and Vinatā. Their husband Kaśyapa, equal to Prajāpati, pleased, filled with the highest joy, granted a boon to those two lawful wives.

sanskrit: varātisargaṃ śrutvaiva kaśyapād uttamaṃ ca te harṣād apratimāṃ prītiṃ prāpatuḥ sma varastriyau
english: Hearing the supremely generous bestowal of boons from Kaśyapa, those two excellent women experienced incomparable delight born of joy.

sanskrit: vavre kadrūḥ sutān nāgān sahasraṃ tulyatejasaḥ dvau putrau vinatā vavre kadrūputrādhikau bale ojasā tejasā caiva vikrameṇādhikau sutau
english: Kadrū chose a thousand serpent sons of equal power; Vinatā chose two sons who would surpass Kadrū's sons in strength, vital force, radiance, and valor.

sanskrit: tasyai bhartā varaṃ prādād adhyardhaṃ putram īpsitam evam astv iti taṃ cāha kaśyapaṃ vinatā tadā
english: Her husband granted her the boon she desired — a son and a half as much again. "So be it," said Vinatā to Kaśyapa then.

sanskrit: kṛtakṛtyā tu vinatā labdhvā vīryādhikau sutau kadrūś ca labdhvā putrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ tulyatejasām
english: Having obtained two sons surpassing in might, Vinatā was fulfilled; and Kadrū, having obtained a thousand sons of equal power —

sanskrit: dhāryau prayatnato garbhāv ity uktvā sa mahātapāḥ te bhārye varasaṃhṛṣṭe kaśyapo vanam āviśat
english: "Bear the embryos with care" — so said that great ascetic; then Kaśyapa, with his two wives elated by the boons, entered the forest.

sanskrit: kālena mahatā kadrūr aṇḍānāṃ daśatīr daśa janayām āsa viprendra dve aṇḍe vinatā tadā
english: After a great length of time, Kadrū laid a hundred clusters of ten eggs; and Vinatā laid two eggs, O chief of brahmins.

sanskrit: tayor aṇḍāni nidadhuḥ prahṛṣṭāḥ paricārikāḥ sopasvedeṣu bhāṇḍeṣu pañca varṣaśatāni ca
english: Their delighted attendants placed the eggs in warm vessels and kept them there for five hundred years.

sanskrit: tataḥ pañcaśate kāle kadrūputrā viniḥsṛtāḥ aṇḍābhyāṃ vinatāyās tu mithunaṃ na vyadṛśyata
english: Then, when five hundred years had passed, Kadrū's sons emerged; but from Vinatā's two eggs no pair of offspring appeared.

sanskrit: tataḥ putrārthiṇī devī vrīḍitā sā tapasvinī aṇḍaṃ bibheda vinatā tatra putram adṛkṣata
english: Then that austerity-practicing goddess, longing for a son and ashamed, broke open one egg; and there she saw a son.

sanskrit: pūrvārdhakāyasaṃpannam itareṇāprakāśatā sa putro roṣasaṃpannaḥ śaśāpainām iti śrutiḥ
english: His upper body was fully formed but the other half was not manifest. That son, filled with anger, cursed her — so the tradition says.

sanskrit: yo 'ham evaṃ kṛto mātas tvayā lobhaparītayā śarīreṇāsamagro 'dya tasmād dāsī bhaviṣyasi
english: "Because you have done this to me, mother, driven by greed, leaving my body incomplete — therefore you shall become a slave."

sanskrit: pañca varṣaśatāny asyā yayā vispardhase saha eṣa ca tvāṃ suto mātar dāsyatvān mokṣayiṣyati
english: "For five hundred years you shall serve her with whom you now rival; and this other son of yours, O mother, shall free you from servitude."

sanskrit: yady enam api mātas tvaṃ mām ivāṇḍavibhedanāt na kariṣyasy adehaṃ vā vyaṅgaṃ vāpi tapasvinam
english: "If you do not, O mother, crack open his egg as you did mine, leaving him bodiless or crippled, that ascetic —"

sanskrit: pratipālayitavyas te janmakālo 'sya dhīrayā viśiṣṭabalam īpsantyā pañcavarṣaśatāt paraḥ
english: "— then you must patiently await his time of birth, you who desire surpassing power, which comes only after five hundred years more."

sanskrit: evaṃ śaptvā tataḥ putro vinatām antarikṣagaḥ aruṇo dṛśyate brahman prabhātasamaye sadā
english: Having thus cursed his mother, that son ascended into the sky; he is seen as Aruṇa, O brahmin, at the break of dawn each day.

sanskrit: garuḍo 'pi yathākālaṃ jajñe pannagasūdanaḥ sa jātamātro vinatāṃ parityajya kham āviśat
english: And Garuḍa too, the destroyer of serpents, was born when his time had come; as soon as he was born he left Vinatā and soared into the sky.

sanskrit: ādāsyann ātmano bhojyam annaṃ vihitam asya yat vidhātrā bhṛguśārdūla kṣudhitasya bubhukṣataḥ
english: He flew off to take for himself the food ordained for him by the Creator, O tiger among Bhṛgus, for he was hungry and longing to eat.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu bhaginyau te tapodhana apaśyatāṃ samāyāntam uccaiḥśravasam antikāt
english: The Sūta said: At this very time, O you rich in austerity, those two sisters saw Uccaiḥśravas approaching from nearby.

sanskrit: yaṃ taṃ devagaṇāḥ sarve hṛṣṭarūpā apūjayan mathyamāne 'mṛte jātam aśvaratnam anuttamam
english: Him all the hosts of gods joyously honored — born when the nectar was being churned, the peerless jewel among horses.

sanskrit: mahaughabalam aśvānām uttamaṃ javatāṃ varam śrīmantam ajaraṃ divyaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam
english: Of surpassing strength among horses, best of the swift, filled with beauty, undecaying, divine, marked with every auspicious sign.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca kathaṃ tad amṛtaṃ devair mathitaṃ kva ca śaṃsa me yatra jajñe mahāvīryaḥ so 'śvarājo mahādyutiḥ
english: Śaunaka said: How did the gods churn that nectar, and where? Tell me the place where that horse-king of great might and great radiance was born.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca jvalantam acalaṃ meruṃ tejorāśim anuttamam ākṣipantaṃ prabhāṃ bhānoḥ svaśṛṅgaiḥ kāñcanojjvalaiḥ
english: The Sūta said: Mount Meru, blazing and unshakeable, that matchless mass of splendor, outshining the sun's own radiance with its gold-gleaming peaks —

sanskrit: kāñcanābharaṇaṃ citraṃ devagandharvasevitam aprameyam anādhṛṣyam adharmabahulair janaiḥ
english: — adorned with golden ornaments, wondrous, attended by gods and gandharvas, immeasurable, unapproachable by those burdened with unrighteousness —

sanskrit: vyālair ācaritaṃ ghorair divyauṣadhividīpitam nākam āvṛtya tiṣṭhantam ucchrayeṇa mahāgirim
english: — roamed by terrible wild beasts, ablaze with divine herbs, that great mountain standing and filling the vault of heaven with its height —

sanskrit: agamyaṃ manasāpy anyair nadīvṛkṣasamanvitam nānāpatagasaṃghaiś ca nāditaṃ sumanoharaiḥ
english: — inaccessible even in thought to others, adorned with rivers and trees, resonant with flocks of many birds, exceedingly beautiful —

sanskrit: tasya pṛṣṭham upāruhya bahuratnācitaṃ śubham anantakalpam udviddhaṃ surāḥ sarve mahaujasaḥ
english: — Climbing its auspicious summit studded with many gems, vast and boundless, all the mighty gods —

sanskrit: te mantrayitum ārabdhās tatrāsīnā divaukasaḥ amṛtārthe samāgamya taponiyamasaṃsthitāḥ
english: — those dwellers in heaven, seated there, began to deliberate, assembled for the purpose of obtaining nectar, established in austerity and restraint.

sanskrit: tatra nārāyaṇo devo brahmāṇam idam abravīt cintayatsu sureṣv evaṃ mantrayatsu ca sarvaśaḥ
english: While the gods were thus deliberating and consulting together on all sides, the divine Nārāyaṇa spoke these words to Brahmā:

sanskrit: devair asurasaṃghaiś ca mathyatāṃ kalaśodadhiḥ bhaviṣyaty amṛtaṃ tatra mathyamāne mahodadhau
english: "Let the ocean, the vessel of waters, be churned by gods together with the hosts of asuras; when the great ocean is churned, nectar shall arise from it."

sanskrit: sarvauṣadhīḥ samāvāpya sarvaratnāni caiva hi manthadhvam udadhiṃ devā vetsyadhvam amṛtaṃ tataḥ
english: "Cast all the herbs and all the jewels into it and churn the ocean, O gods — then you shall obtain the nectar from it."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tato 'bhraśikharākārair giriśṛṅgair alaṃkṛtam mandaraṃ parvatavaraṃ latājālasamāvṛtam
english: The Sūta said: Then Mount Mandara, that foremost of mountains, adorned with peaks shaped like cloud-tops, wrapped in nets of creepers —
